messages:
Marta Chen: Heads up — SIEM stream 'kms_access_failure' spiked ~600/hr starting ~18:05 UTC. Mostly service-account CI tokens hitting key-access and getting AccessDenied. Any recent RBAC/KMS policy changes?
Liam O'Connor: I see the same on the alert dashboard. Quick query I ran: 
```
index=siem sourcetype=kms event=kms_access_failure | stats count by source_service, error_code, key_id
```
Top sources look like ci-runner-*-staging. error_code=AccessDenied.
Jae Park: We pushed a tightening change to the KMS key bindings last night for project-x (removed broad runner role). Could be that. @Priya Nair did you deploy that?
Priya Nair: Yep, I rotated the key policy at 03:02 UTC to remove an old binding. I thought only prod had that runner role; looks like staging got affected too. Opening a revert PR now.
Sam Ortiz: Suggest we add a short-lived SIEM suppression for staging to avoid alert fatigue while we fix RBAC. Also propose updating the rule to ignore known CI service-account patterns (ci-runner-.*) for AccessDenied events unless they exceed a high-volume threshold.
Tara Liu: We should also enrich the alerts with the audit_log_link and principal_email to speed triage. Can we pipe in Cloud Audit log id as context?
Marta Chen: Agreed. Quick mitigation plan: 1) suppression for staging (1 hour), 2) add exception for ci-runner-.* for AccessDenied, 3) update the dashboard to surface top key_ids and principal emails. Can someone set the suppression?
DevSecBot: Incident created INC-2026-488 by Marta Chen. Assigned: eng-security, devops. Priority: P3. Link: https://redwood.example/incident/INC-2026-488 :white_check_mark:
Priya Nair: PR opened to restore runner binding: https://git.internal/rb/changes/4523. Will apply as soon as CI gating passes.
Liam O'Connor: For the SIEM rule change, propose this pseudo-filter: 
```
when event.type == "kms_access_failure" and error_code == "AccessDenied":
  if principal =~ /ci-runner-.*/ and env == "staging":
    suppress for 60m unless count(principal, window=10m) > 50
  else:
    alert
```
That keeps noisy staging CI from filling the channel but still catches abnormal spikes.
Sam Ortiz: Can we instead make the rule alert only if the same principal produces >20 AccessDenied within 10m AND key_id not in exception-list? That catches runaway jobs while ignoring expected one-offs.
Jae Park: RBAC fix deployed (changes/4523 merged, binding re-added). IAM propagation might take a couple minutes. Priya, can you confirm once you see successful key access from a runner?
Priya Nair: Watching logs. I see initial successes coming through for ci-runner-12 at 18:27 UTC. Rolling back confirmed.
Tara Liu: I added a dashboard tile: Top 20 principals for AccessDenied and linked the audit_log_id field to cloud console. Also added a facet for key_id.
Marta Chen: Nice. Sam/Liam, can one of you file a small rule-tuning PR with the suppress+thresholds we discussed and include a note to re-run after 24h to evaluate?
Sam Ortiz: On it — will submit a PR to SIEM rules repo with tests. PR link when ready.
DevSecBot: SIEM suppression rule created: suppression_id=SUPP-987 (applies to env=staging, principal =~ /ci-runner-.*/, duration=60m).
Liam O'Connor: PR for rule-tuning created: https://git.internal/siem/rules/789 (adds threshold logic + exception-list for known CI keys). Includes unit tests against replay logs.
Marta Chen: Outstanding followups: 1) keep suppression until we confirm no further RBAC churn, 2) Sam to merge rule PR and monitor, 3) Tara to keep dashboard live, 4) DevSec to add runbook steps for KMS access failures.
Jae Park: Adding a small automated check in our infra CI to verify KMS bindings for runner roles on key changes (prevent future accidental removals). Will open infra PR.
Priya Nair: Confirmed runners healthy. Closing the incident once suppression expires unless we see fresh alerts.
Marta Chen: Thanks all — good cross-team work. Will follow up with a short postmortem note under INC-2026-488 documenting the RBAC drift and the SIEM tuning we applied. :memo:
